lines.say: What's that stabbing pain in your side when you run?
It's called a side stitch. And scientists still aren't fully sure.
In one survey, about seven in ten runners had at least one in a year.
The leading theory: the lining inside your belly wall gets irritated.
A full stomach rubbing and bouncing may make it worse.
That's why stitches are more common after a big meal or a big drink.
Try this: eat or drink lightly in the two hours before you run.
If it hits, slow down, breathe deeply, and press on the spot.
Next time: why does your face go red when you lift?
